identity.title: ProtComposer: Compositional Protein Structure Generation with 3D Ellipsoids

problem.claim: Generate protein structures conditioned on spatial layouts describing substructure shapes and semantics.

gap.claim: Existing generative models commonly oversample conceptually simple helix bundles, limiting matching of PDB-like helix fractions.

contributions.claim: ProtComposer conditions protein-structure generation on layouts represented by 3D ellipsoids.
The method supports ellipsoids that are hand-constructed, extracted from existing proteins, or sampled from a statistical model, enabling distinct control, redesign, and generation uses.
The authors report improved Pareto frontiers across designability, novelty, and diversity, plus sampling of designable proteins with PDB-matching helix fractions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce compositional protein generation through 3D ellipsoids that encode substructure shape and semantics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved trade-off frontiers among designability, novelty, and diversity when conditioning on novel, diverse layouts from a simple statistical model.
The authors report that the approach can sample designable proteins whose helix fraction matches that of PDB proteins, unlike commonly observed behavior in existing generative models.

narrative_sequence.summary: ProtComposer is introduced for protein generation conditioned on spatial layouts encoded by 3D ellipsoids.
Different ellipsoid sources provide user control, redesign of existing structures, or statistically generated layouts.
Statistical-model layouts are reported to expand designability–novelty–diversity trade-offs and better match PDB helix fractions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps three conditioning-data sources to distinct capabilities: manual control, existing-protein editing, and statistical-layout exploration.

lessons.interpretation: Separating input provenance from the capability it enables makes a compositional method's use cases concrete.
lessons.application: When presenting a controllable generative system, organize the method around a small set of input-construction modes and state the capability unlocked by each.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when input modes do not produce meaningfully different behaviors or use cases.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify evaluation datasets, baselines, metric values, or the conditions under which the reported improvements were measured.
The abstract does not describe the statistical model or how ellipsoid layouts are extracted and converted into generated structures.
